How to Apply Online for RITES Apprentices Recruitment 2026?

Step 1 - Register and Apply through NATS or NAPS

  1. Visit the NATS portal if you are an Engineering Graduate, Non-Engineering Graduate or Diploma candidate.
  2. ITI candidates should visit the NAPS Apprenticeship India portal.
  3. Complete student or candidate registration if not already registered.
  4. Log in and complete the apprenticeship profile.
  5. Verify personal details, category, educational qualifications and aggregate percentage.
  6. Search the available apprenticeship opportunities using the establishment name RITES Limited.
  7. Select the relevant apprenticeship opportunity matching your qualification or trade.
  8. Submit the application through the appropriate portal.
  9. Save the NATS or NAPS application details and registration number.

Step 2 - Submit the RITES Apprentice Application Form

  1. Visit the official RITES Apprentice Application Form.
  2. Complete the form using the information requested by RITES.
  3. Prepare all required educational qualification certificates and identity documents.
  4. Include the applicable category certificate where reservation is claimed.
  5. Include the university or institution's CGPA conversion formula where required.
  6. Combine all prescribed documents into one PDF file not exceeding 10 MB.
  7. Upload the combined PDF through the RITES application form.
  8. Indicate the preferred posting location if the form provides that option.
  9. Review the submitted information and document file carefully.
  10. Complete the form in a single submission by 25 November 2026.
  11. Retain your apprenticeship registration and application details for future communication.

Important: RITES does not accept multiple submissions of the document form. Supporting documents submitted by email or hard copy will not be considered.

  • The combined PDF must not exceed 10 MB.

  • Hard-copy document submissions are not accepted at the application stage.
  • Documents not requested in the notification should not be uploaded.
  • Applicants must submit the required documents by 25 November 2026.

OBC Non-Creamy Layer candidates must submit a valid caste certificate in the prescribed Government of India Central format, issued on or after 5 November 2025.

EWS candidates must provide the latest applicable EWS certificate in the prescribed format.

Candidates claiming SC, ST, OBC-NCL, EWS or PwBD reservation must submit valid documents supporting their claim.

RITES Apprentice PwBD Reservation 2026

The notification includes four PwBD reservation positions on a horizontal basis. Applicants seeking PwBD benefits must possess a certificate issued by the competent authority.

Candidates must have at least 40% of the relevant disability and satisfy the physical requirements and functional classifications applicable to the selected apprenticeship position.

PwBD reservation is included within the advertised vacancies and must not be added separately.

RITES Apprentice Posting Location 2026

The apprenticeship opportunities are available across India. Candidates from all states are eligible to apply, subject to the prescribed qualifications and other requirements.

Applicants may provide their preferred location through the RITES application form. However, the final posting will be determined by the company's operational requirements.

Important: A preferred location does not guarantee posting at that location. RITES will not entertain subsequent requests to change the posting preference after the prescribed process.

RITES Apprentice Merit List 2026

RITES will prepare the merit list after examining apprenticeship applications submitted through NATS or NAPS and verifying documents submitted through the RITES form.

Shortlisted candidates will receive instructions through email from [email protected]. The selected candidates list will also be uploaded on the official RITES website.

Candidates must bring the original documents at the time of joining for further verification.

Vacancies remaining unfilled after the initial shortlisting process may be filled from subsequent merit lists of eligible candidates.

Common Reasons for Rejection of RITES Apprentice Applications

  • Applicant is below 18 years as on 5 November 2026.
  • Essential qualification result is pending on the cut-off date.
  • Degree or diploma passing date is before 5 November 2021.
  • Candidate has already completed or is undergoing apprenticeship training.
  • Candidate has one year or more of post-qualification work or training experience.
  • Minimum aggregate percentage requirement is not satisfied.
  • Application is not submitted through the correct NATS or NAPS portal.
  • Candidate fails to apply for the RITES Limited establishment.
  • Mandatory RITES document form is not submitted.
  • Required documents are missing or invalid.
  • CGPA conversion formula is missing where applicable.
  • OBC-NCL or EWS certificate does not meet the prescribed requirements.
  • Application contains false or inconsistent information.
  • Required original documents cannot be produced at joining.

RBI Grade B Final Cut Off 2026 Explained

The final cut off is the minimum combined score needed for selection in each category. It is calculated out of 375 marks.

  • The interview carries 75 marks.
  • Phase 1 is qualifying in nature and does not add marks to the final merit.

The General category final cut off is 241.25, the OBC final cut off is 229.75, the ST final cut off is 226.25, the SC final cut off is 224.00 and the EWS final cut off is 217.50.

RBI Grade B Selection Process and Marks Scheme

The selection for Officers in Grade 'B' (DR) has three stages.

  1. Phase 1 (Prelims): qualifying in nature.
  2. Phase 2 (Mains): 300 marks. For the General stream, the papers are Paper I (Economic and Social Issues), Paper II (English) and Paper III (Finance and Management).
  3. Phase 3 (Interview): 75 marks.

Final selection depends on the combined score of Phase 2 and the interview, out of 375 marks. The paper structure for the DEPR and DSIM streams is not covered here.

What Affects the RBI Grade B Phase 2 Cut Off?

  • Number of vacancies: a larger number of posts allows more candidates to be called for the interview.
  • Difficulty of the papers: especially the descriptive English and subject papers.
  • Overall performance of candidates: higher average scores push the cut off up.
  • Category-wise competition: each category has its own cut off.

The RBI Grade B General Cadre selection process comprises three main stages:

Only domiciles of the UT of Ladakh can apply for the 21 Banking Associate posts advertised by Jammu & Kashmir Bank Ltd. (J&K Bank) under advertisement PO-Jobs2026@JKBank. Candidates must be graduates in any discipline and aged 20 to 30 years as on 01-01-2026. Applications are accepted only online through the Bank's website jkb.bank.in under the "Careers" tab from 7 November 2026 to 26 November 2026, and the online examination will be conducted by IBPS.

J&K Bank Banking Associates at a Glance

Particulars Details
Organisation Jammu & Kashmir Bank Ltd., Corporate Headquarters, M.A. Road, Srinagar
Advertisement No. PO-Jobs2026@JKBank
Post Name Banking Associate
Vacancies 21
Who Can Apply Only domiciles of the UT of Ladakh
Age Limit Minimum 20 years, maximum 30 years (as on 01-01-2026)
Application Fee Rs. 600/- (excluding GST) for SC/ST/SEBC/PwBD/ESM; Rs. 800/- (excluding GST) for all others
Job Location Branch/Office(s) of the Ladakh Zone
Application Mode Online
Last Date to Apply 26-11-2026

The official notification does not specify the pay for the post.

About J&K Bank Banking Associates

Jammu & Kashmir Bank Ltd. has its Corporate Headquarters on M.A. Road, Srinagar. This recruitment, titled "Recruitment of Banking Associates – UT of Ladakh", fills posts for the Bank's Branch/Office(s) in the Ladakh Zone, and the online examination is conducted by IBPS.

Who Can Apply

Domicile

Only domiciles of the UT of Ladakh are eligible to apply. Selected candidates will have to submit the domicile certificate of the UT of Ladakh issued by the competent authority.

Educational Qualification

  • Graduate in any discipline from a university recognized by Government of India, or any other equivalent qualification recognized as such by the Central Government/UGC, as on the last date of registration.
  • The candidate must possess a valid marks sheet/degree certificate showing that he/she is a graduate as on the last date of registration, and must indicate the percentage of marks obtained in Graduation while registering online.
  • The percentage is to be calculated to the nearest two decimals. Where CGPA/OGPA is awarded, it must be converted into percentage, and a certificate from the appropriate authority on the University's conversion norms must be produced.
  • Percentage is calculated on total marks in all subjects in all semesters/years divided by the aggregate maximum marks (including honours/optional/additional optional subjects), multiplied by 100. Fractions are ignored: 59.99% is treated as less than 60%.

Candidates should check the official notification for the complete eligibility conditions of the post.

Age Limit

Minimum: 20 years, Maximum: 30 years as on 01-01-2026. A candidate must have been born not earlier than 01.01.1996 and not later than 01.01.2006 (both dates inclusive). The maximum age limit applies to General and EWS category candidates.

Reservation and Age Relaxation

Reservation follows the Union territory of Ladakh Reservation Rules, 2005 and S.O. 77 dated June 27, 2025 of the Social & Tribal Welfare Department, Administration of UT of Ladakh. The notice gives reservation as percentages; it does not print category-wise numbers of the 21 posts.

Category Reservation Age Relaxation
Scheduled Castes 1% 5 years
Scheduled Tribes 80% 5 years
Socially and Educationally Backward Classes (Residents of areas adjoining the Actual Line of Control in UT of Ladakh) 4% 5 years
Economically Weaker Sections (EWSs) 10% Nil
Ex-servicemen 6% (Horizontal) Period of actual military service deducted from actual age; eligible if resultant age exceeds the maximum by not more than three years
Persons with benchmark disabilities 4% (Horizontal) 10 years
Outstanding Sportspersons 4% (Horizontal) Not specified in the notice
  • The maximum age for Ex-Servicemen is capped at 48 years after relaxation.
  • SC/ST/SEBC relaxation is allowed cumulatively with the relaxation for persons with benchmark disabilities.
  • Apprentices who completed Apprenticeship Training with J&K Bank and are domiciles of UT of Ladakh get 1 year of age relaxation in addition to their category relaxation, plus additional marks equal to 2.5% of the maximum marks in the online examination.
  • Within the 4% for benchmark disabilities, 1% each is for (a) blindness or low vision, (b) deaf and hard of hearing, (c) locomotor disability including cerebral palsy, leprosy cured, dwarfism, acid attack victims and muscular dystrophy, and (d) autism, intellectual disability, specific learning disability and mental illness; clause (e) covers multiple disabilities.
  • PwBD candidates whose certificate shows a temporary disability "likely to improve" are not eligible for reservation.
  • Outstanding Sportspersons must upload a certificate in the format prescribed under the UT of Ladakh Outstanding Sportspersons Rules at registration.
  • Unfilled EWS vacancies will be treated as unreserved. The category certificate must be valid on the date of online registration, and the EWS certificate must be valid for the year 2026-2027.

How to Apply for J&K Bank Banking Associates

Applications are accepted online only from 7 November 2026 to 26 November 2026; no other mode is accepted. Registration is complete only when the fee is successfully paid online.

  1. Go to https://jkb.bank.in/, open the relevant notification under the "Careers" tab and click "APPLY ONLINE".
  2. Choose "Click here for New Registration" and enter name, contact details and email-id; note the Provisional Registration Number and Password sent by email and SMS.
  3. Click "Validate your details" and "Save & Next"; the "SAVE AND NEXT" facility lets you complete the form in more than one sitting.
  4. Upload the photograph, signature, left thumb impression and handwritten declaration, and capture a live photograph by webcam or mobile phone.
  5. Fill the other details, preview the form and click "COMPLETE REGISTRATION"; no change is possible after this.
  6. Click the "Payment" tab, pay the fee and click "Submit".
  7. Print the e-Receipt and the online application form containing fee details.

Application Fee

Category Fee
SC/ST/SEBC/PwBD/ESM Rs. 600/- (excluding GST)
All others Rs. 800/- (excluding GST)

The fee is paid online from 07.11.2026 to 26.11.2026 (both dates inclusive) by Debit Cards (RuPay/Visa/MasterCard/Maestro), Credit Cards, Internet Banking, IMPS or Cash Cards/Mobile Wallets. Bank transaction charges are borne by the candidate. If no e-Receipt is generated, the payment has failed and must be repeated after logging in again.

Image Specifications

Item Specification
Photograph (4.5cm × 3.5cm) Recent colour passport-style, light background; 200 x 230 pixels (preferred); 20kb–50kb
Signature Black ink on white paper; 140 x 60 pixels (preferred); 10kb–20kb; not in capital letters

The declaration text is: "I, _______ (Name of the candidate), hereby declare that all the information submitted by me in the application form is correct, true and valid. I will present the supporting documents as and when required." It must be in the candidate's own handwriting; visually impaired candidates who cannot write may type it and put their left thumb impression below it.

Documents named in the notice

  • 10th Certificate (Marksheet/Passing Certificate)
  • Graduation Certificate (Degree/Consolidated Marksheet)
  • Apprenticeship Completion Certificate, if applicable
  • Ex-Servicemen Certificate, if applicable
  • Certificate/s of Disability as per Form-I, II and III, and the Appendix I certificate on physical limitation to write, if applicable
  • Certificate under the UT of Ladakh Outstanding Sportspersons Rules, if applicable

Documents are uploaded in PDF only, each file not exceeding 500 kb, with one single file for educational certificates.

Selection Process

Selection is through an online examination; marks obtained in the online examination only are considered for shortlisting/provisional selection, according to the reservation rules and subject to all other selection parameters. Documents in original with a photocopy are verified before provisional appointment letters are issued.

Test Questions Marks Medium Duration
English Language 30 30 English 20 Minutes
Quantitative Aptitude 35 30 English 20 Minutes
Reasoning Ability 35 40 English 20 Minutes
Total 100 100 60 Minutes
  • Each test is separately timed, and candidates must qualify in each of the three tests by securing cut-off marks decided by IBPS with J&K Bank.
  • Negative marking: one fourth of the marks assigned to a question is deducted for each wrong answer; blank questions carry no penalty.
  • Cut-offs are applied on individual test scores and on the total score. The minimum aggregate qualifying marks are 40% for General Category and 35% for reserved category candidates, subject to overall merit.
  • Scores are equated across sessions and reported up to two decimal points. Ties are broken by date of birth, with the older candidate placed ahead.

Examination Centres

Candidates must choose six centres, at least four of them outside Ladakh-UT. Within Ladakh-UT: Leh and Kargil. Outside Ladakh-UT: Delhi NCR, Patiala, Mohali, Ludhiana, Amritsar, Pathankot, Jalandhar, Bengaluru, Phagwara and others if need arise. The Bank may allot a centre other than those opted, and no request for change of centre, venue, date or session will be entertained.

Important Instructions

  • Selected candidates must remain posted within the Branch/Office(s) of the Ladakh Zone for a minimum of 5 years; no transfer outside the allotted Zone is permitted before that period on any ground.
  • Candidates must give a self-declaration of character and antecedents in a prescribed format; the appointing authority may reject or cancel candidature for material misrepresentation or conviction in a criminal offence involving moral turpitude.
  • No change of category is permitted after registration.
  • At the examination and at joining, bring the call letter with an original and a photocopy of a valid photo identity bearing exactly the same name; Ration Card and Learner's Driving License are not accepted.
  • Candidates reporting after the time on the call letter will not be allowed to take the examination; candidates may need to be at the venue for about 4 hours.
  • PwBD candidates using a scribe must arrange their own scribe, upload the Appendix I certificate and submit the Appendix II undertaking at the examination; compensatory time of 20 minutes per hour applies to eligible candidates registered for it.
  • Keep a valid personal email ID and mobile number active till the recruitment ends; call letter intimations may be sent by email.

Punjab & Sind Bank (a Govt. of India Undertaking), through its Head Office HRD Department in New Delhi, is engaging one Chief Risk Officer (CRO) on contract for professional services. The initial tenure is three years, the age limit is 40 years minimum and less than 55 years (as on 01.11.2026), and the pay is to be negotiated. Applications are online only at punjabandsind.bank.in from 7 November 2026 to 17 November 2026; the time of closing is not printed.

About PSB

Punjab & Sind Bank describes itself as a Govt. of India Undertaking, with its Head Office HRD Department at NBCC Building Block 3, Kidwai Nagar, New Delhi - 110023. The Chief Risk Officer will oversee risk management across the Bank, including at group level covering Domestic Operations, Domestic Subsidiaries and Branches.

Who Can Apply

Nationality

A candidate must be a citizen of India, a subject of Nepal or Bhutan, a Tibetan refugee who came to India before 1 January 1962 intending to settle permanently, or a person of Indian origin who migrated from Pakistan, Burma, Sri Lanka, Kenya, Uganda, the United Republic of Tanzania, Zambia, Malawi, Zaire, Ethiopia or Vietnam intending to settle permanently. The last four groups need a certificate of eligibility issued by the Govt. of India.

Essential qualification and experience (as on 17.11.2026)

  • Graduate Degree from a university/institution recognised by the Government of India or its regulatory bodies.
  • At least five years' experience in Corporate Credit and Risk Management at the level of Assistant General Manager or above in one or more Public Sector Banks; or in an equivalent senior position, with similar roles and responsibilities, in one or more regulated lending entities, as may be determined by the Bank and the CRO Selection Committee, with minimum experience of one year in Corporate Credit and one year in Risk Management.
  • Along with any one of: (a) professional certification in financial risk management from the Global Association of Risk Professionals; (b) Professional Risk Management Certification from the PRMIA Institute; or at least two years' experience as Chief Risk Officer in a regulated lending entity where the CRO must be appointed with Board approval under a regulatory requirement.

Desirable

Preference may be given to candidates with one or more of the following:

  • Chartered Financial Analyst charter from the CFA Institute.
  • Chartered Accountant qualification from the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India or an equivalent qualification obtained abroad.
  • Cost and Management Accountant qualification from the Institute of Cost Accountants of India or an equivalent qualification obtained abroad.
  • Postgraduate degree in Finance, Economics, Banking, Risk Management, Business Administration or a related field.
  • Certification or specialised qualification in treasury risk, credit risk, operational risk, cyber risk, climate risk, data analytics or model-risk management.
  • Desirable experience: good understanding of market risk and/or liquidity management and/or operational risk, with exposure to analytics an added advantage.

Age limit

Minimum 40 years of age and less than 55 years of age (as on 01.11.2026). The notice prints no age relaxation. Date of birth as per the Secondary School Certificate (SSC)/School leaving certificate must confirm age eligibility.

Pay and Terms

  • Pay: the compensation and terms and conditions will be negotiated/finalised depending upon the suitability of the candidate.
  • Tenure: the CRO may initially be engaged for a fixed contractual tenure of three years, extendable by one year at a time, up to a maximum of five years, subject to annual performance review by the Board/Risk Management Committee of the Board.
  • The engagement is purely contractual and gives no right to claim regular employment or absorption in the Bank.
  • Working hours and weekly off/holidays are as applicable to the Bank's serving employees.
  • Leave: 30 days' paid leave per calendar year, not more than 05 days at a time. Absence beyond 30 days in a contract year leads to a proportionate deduction from the consolidated payment, and unavailed leave lapses at the end of the contract year.
  • PF, Gratuity, Pension etc. do not apply, and no other allowance, payment, benefit or facility is payable beyond what the notice mentions.
  • Location: preferably Head Office/Corporate Office; the Bank reserves the right to post the candidate to any office in India depending on administrative requirements.

PSB CHIEF RISK OFFICER Job Description

The CRO oversees the entire risk management process of the Bank, including at group level, reviews risk models, and develops policies, procedures and pricing models. The role is grouped under credit risk, market risk, operational risk, and liquidity and interest rate risk management, and also includes RBI guidelines applicable from time to time. Annexure I of the notice lists these duties:

  • Act as risk assessor and overall in charge of the Bank's Risk Management function, and advise top management.
  • Implement and maintain an enterprise-wide integrated risk management and governance framework covering credit, investment, operational, market and compliance risk.
  • Report the Bank's risk profile periodically to Risk Committees, top management and the Board, and implement BASEL guidelines as per RBI directives.
  • Oversee the Fraud Risk Management Department (FRMD) and strengthen frameworks including EIRMS, policy and cyber risk governance.
  • Credit risk: bank-wide credit risk management, risk limits and risk appetite, stress testing, preparation of the Annual ICAAP document, monitoring of large exposures, and validation of Credit Risk Assessment (CRA)/scoring models.
  • Market risk: turn the Board's framework into policies and procedures, and guide the market risk team on interest rate risk, equity price risk, derivatives, country limits, counterparty bank limits and stress testing.
  • Operational risk: supervise the ORM Cell, review operational risk policies, conduct the Product and Process Approval Committee, Credit Policy Committee, ALCO and ORMC meetings, oversee AML/CFT controls and IT security risk, and ensure Board RMC meetings are held as scheduled.
  • Liquidity and interest rate risk: oversee the liquidity position of all PSB Zones and departments, supervise the ALM Cell and review the Asset Liability Management Policy.

The notice adds that any other roles and responsibilities may be assigned by the authorities/Bank.

How to Apply for PSB CHIEF RISK OFFICER

  1. Log on to the Bank's website https://punjabandsind.bank.in/ and, on the Home Page under the link "Recruitment", click the relevant Notification. No other mode of application is accepted.
  2. Before registering, keep a valid personal email ID and mobile number active until the appointment process ends. Call letters are sent to the registered email ID.
  3. Spell your name and your father's/husband's name exactly as in your certificates, mark sheets and identity proof. Any change found may disqualify the candidature.
  4. Pay the application fee online only. Cash, Demand Drafts, Cheques, Money Orders and Postal Stamps are not accepted.
  5. Submit the application by 17.11.2026. Applications received after the stipulated date and incomplete applications are rejected.

Application fee

The fee is Rs. 1000/- + GST as applicable. The table prints Rs. 1180/- (including CGST and SGST) for New Delhi and Rs. 1180/- (including IGST) for out of New Delhi. Transaction charges are borne by the candidate. The fee is non-refundable and cannot be held in reserve for any other selection. An application cannot be withdrawn once made.

Documents named in the notice

  • Scanned photograph and signature as per the guidelines in the advertisement; image formats .png, .jpg, .jpeg, .bmp, .gif.
  • Scanned thumb impression and handwritten declaration: "I, _______ (Name of the candidate), hereby declare that all the information submitted by me in the application form is correct, true and valid. I will present the supporting documents as and when required."
  • Education, experience, reservation certificates and date of birth proof, scanned in PDF format only.
  • Original documents at the interview; candidates will not be allowed to participate without them. Copies of the same passport-size photograph are to be brought for the interview.

Selection Process

The selection process may broadly comprise preliminary scrutiny of applications, shortlisting, a personal interaction/interview before the Selection Committee, and verification of credentials. Final selection is on marks obtained in the interview, by merit ranking.

  • Scrutiny: applications are checked against age, qualifications, experience and other eligibility conditions.
  • Shortlisting: based on relevant experience, seniority, professional credentials and suitability, and on academic track record. Only shortlisted candidates are called. Meeting the minimum qualification and experience gives no right to be called.
  • Interview: assesses knowledge of credit, market, operational, liquidity, technology, cyber, climate and other material risks, plus leadership ability, independence of judgement, regulatory awareness and ability to interact with the Board and senior management.
  • Verification of credentials, vigilance status, integrity, reputation and antecedents.

The interview venue, date and time will be informed in the call letter, sent by email only. Candidates attend at their own cost. The notice mentions no written test.

Important Instructions

  • Candidates serving in Government/Public Sector Undertakings including Banks must produce a No Objection Certificate from their employer at the time of interview, failing which the candidature will not be considered.
  • The selected candidate must produce a valid discharge/relieving letter from the present employer before joining.
  • Appointment is subject to medical fitness, the required qualifications and experience, and clearances, verifications and background checks.
  • The number of vacancies is provisional and may vary with the Bank's requirement.
  • If several applications are made, only the last valid complete application is retained.
  • Requests to change the interview date, time or venue will not be entertained.
  • The Bank may change, add or cancel the selection process, or cancel the whole process, and will announce this on its website or by email.
  • False information or suppressed facts lead to cancellation, forfeiture of fee and possible termination after appointment. Canvassing in any form is a disqualification.
  • Any dispute is subject to the sole jurisdiction of the Courts at Delhi, and the English version prevails.

  • In case of selection, candidates will be required to produce a proper discharge certificate from their current employer at the time of taking up the engagement.

SBI Recruitment 2026 Job Description

GM & Chief AI Officer

Job Profile and Key Responsibilities:

  • Lead the implementation and operations of Machine Learning, Artificial Intelligence, Natural Language Processing, and parsing tools to improve operational efficiency and mitigate risk.
  • Design and implement big data scalable workflow systems including Enterprise AI Platform for generative and agentic AI.
  • Deliver AI solutions at scale with operational and analytical integrations including Cloudera Data Lakehouse and enterprise API platforms.
  • Deliver new functionality for internal production and client delivery platforms.
  • Collaborate with Product Management, Business, Quality Assurance, Data Operation, and IT Infrastructure.
  • Oversee business collaboration via permanent control towers for AI/data products and ensure seamless integration into formal business processes.
  • Ensure compliance with internal and regulatory norms and align with Bank governance standards and top management directives.
  • Oversee independent model validation team and evaluate ongoing risk and performance in models.

DGM (Risk and Operational Analytics)

Job Profile and Key Responsibilities:

  • Lead the Bank's risk and operational analytics function and establish an enterprise-wide roadmap across Risk, Compliance, Business, and Operations.
  • Lead design, development, validation, implementation, and operations of AI/ML models for early-warning systems, collections, fraud prevention, operational risk, financial risk, and process optimization.
  • Integrate analytical models and decision engines into core banking, loan origination, and operational workflows via enterprise data and API platforms.
  • Establish human-in-the-loop controls, override mechanisms, audit trails, and escalation procedures for material decisions.
  • Prioritise high-impact use cases based on loss reduction, regulatory importance, customer impact, efficiency, and feasibility.
  • Drive responsible adoption of generative and agentic AI for risk intelligence, document analysis, and operational decision support.

DGM (AI Governance and Compliance)

Job Profile and Key Responsibilities:

  • Lead the Bank's AI governance and compliance function across ML, generative AI, and agentic AI.
  • Develop, maintain, and enforce AI governance policies, standards, risk-classification methodologies, and control frameworks.
  • Oversee independent validation, periodic review, and governance controls for material models and AI-enabled systems.
  • Ensure compliance with applicable RBI directions, Digital Personal Data Protection Act and Rules, and information security norms.
  • Coordinate AI risk assessments, privacy impact assessments, security reviews, and approval processes before production deployment.
  • Oversee third-party AI governance, vendor due diligence, contractual safeguards, and data-use restrictions.
  • Convene or support governance committees and coordinate regulatory inspections and audit closures.

DGM (Data Engineering, Model Application Dev and AI Ops)

Job Profile and Key Responsibilities:

  • Lead data engineering, model application development, and AI Ops functions to deliver scalable, secure data and AI pipelines.
  • Design, develop, and operate enterprise data pipelines, model-serving platforms, and APIs in coordination with GITC.
  • Establish engineering standards for MLOps, LLMOps, DevSecOps, testing, CI/CD, and release management.
  • Automate deployment, monitoring, rollback, recalibration, and retirement for AI/ML models and agentic AI applications.
  • Implement observability covering availability, latency, throughput, data quality, performance, capacity, and compute utilisation.
  • Manage technology vendors, systems integrators, and platform providers.

AI Solution Architect

Job Profile and Key Responsibilities:

  • Partner with business units and technology teams to identify, conceptualize, design, and implement scalable AI solutions.
  • Translate business requirements into AI solution concepts, functional blueprints, and user journeys.
  • Collaborate with engineers, data scientists, enterprise architects, and application teams to develop implementable technical designs.
  • Define AI risk controls, guardrails, human-in-the-loop mechanisms, and explainability requirements.
  • Support development of business cases, evaluate alternative approaches, and guide PoCs and pilots.
  • Create reusable solution patterns, templates, and blueprints for common AI use cases across the Bank.

Enterprise AI Architect

Job Profile and Key Responsibilities:

  • Define, govern, and evolve the Bank's enterprise AI architecture strategy and on-premises NVIDIA-based AI platform.
  • Design and optimize GPU infrastructure and workload architectures leveraging NVIDIA AI Enterprise ecosystem.
  • Lead architectural design of Generative AI, LLM solutions, RAG, and vector databases.
  • Establish MLOps/LLMOps pipelines, model gateways, model serving mechanisms, and API integration strategies.
  • Architect secure and scalable enterprise data platforms and enforce technology standards, security, resilience, and disaster recovery.
  • Conduct architecture reviews and manage architecture exceptions.

How to Apply for SBI Recruitment 2026

Candidates must submit their applications online through the official careers portal of State Bank of India. No hard copy of the application or documents needs to be sent by post.

  1. Visit the official SBI careers portal and navigate to the current openings page.
  2. Locate the link for Specialist Cadre Officers recruitment under advertisement CRPD/SCO/2026-27/30.
  3. Register online by entering basic details to generate a provisional registration number and password. The facility for editing saved application details is available up to three times only before final submission.
  4. Fill in the online application form carefully with educational, professional, and personal details.
  5. Upload scanned copies of photograph, signature, biodata, resume, ID proof, age proof, educational certificates, experience certificates, salary slips/Form-16, and other required documents in the prescribed format and size.
  6. Pay the non-refundable application fee of Rs. 750/- (exempted for SC/ST/PwBD) online using Internet Banking, Debit Card, Credit Card, or UPI.
  7. Submit the completed application form and print a copy of the system-generated application form and e-receipt for future reference.

Document Upload Specifications:

  • Photograph: Recent passport style colour picture (20 kb to 50 kb, JPG/JPEG format, preferred dimensions 200 x 230 pixels, light-coloured or white background).
  • Signature: Signed on white paper with Black Ink pen (10 kb to 20 kb, JPG/JPEG format, preferred dimensions 140 x 60 pixels; signatures in capital letters are not accepted).
  • Other Documents: Biodata, Resume, ID proof, Proof of Date of Birth, Educational Certificates, Experience Certificates, Caste/EWS/PwBD certificate (if applicable), Form-16/Offer Letter/Latest Salary Slip, and CTC negotiation sheet must be uploaded in PDF format on A4 size, with file size not exceeding 500 kb each.

Queries: For any queries, candidates can write via the "CONTACT US/ Post Your Query" link available on the Bank's website (https://sbi.bank.in/web/careers/post-your-query) or email [email protected].

Selection and Interview

The selection process comprises three stages: Shortlisting, Interview, and CTC Negotiation.

  • Shortlisting: Fulfilling minimum eligibility criteria does not guarantee a call for interview. The shortlisting committee constituted by the Bank will decide shortlisting parameters to call an adequate number of candidates.
  • Interview (100 Marks): The interview carries 100 marks. For the posts of GM & Chief AI officer, DGM (Risk and Operational Analytics), DGM (AI Governance and Compliance), and DGM (Data Engineering, Model Application Dev and AI Ops), shortlisted candidates must deliver a 10-minute presentation on their relevant job profile, projects undertaken, or milestones achieved. Qualifying marks in the interview are decided by the Bank. Intimation or call letters for the interview will be uploaded on the Bank's website or sent by email; no hard copy will be sent.
  • CTC Negotiation: CTC negotiation is conducted one-by-one with candidates at the time of interview or separately after the interview process.
  • Merit List: The final merit list is prepared in descending order based solely on scores obtained in the interview. In case of a tie in cut-off marks, candidates are ranked according to age in descending order.

Travelling Allowance for Interview: Outstation candidates called for interview after shortlisting will be reimbursed the cost of travelling by Air fare (Economy Class) for the shortest route in India as follows:

  • GM & Chief AI officer and all three DGM posts (Sl. No. 1 to 4): Reimbursement of actual Air Fare (Economy Class).
  • AI Solution Architect and Enterprise AI Architect (Sl. No. 5 & 6): Reimbursement of Air Fare up to Rs. 15,000/- (Total for both sides) or actual fare, whichever is lower.
  • Note: In case a candidate called for interview is found not satisfying the eligibility criteria (Age, Educational Qualification, Experience, etc.), he/she will neither be allowed to appear for the interview nor be entitled to reimbursement of any travelling expenses.

About NaBFID

The National Bank for Financing Infrastructure and Development (NaBFID) has been set up under an Act of Parliament, the NaBFID Act, 2021, as the principal entity for infrastructure financing in the country. It is regulated and supervised as an All-India Financial Institution (AIFI) by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI). According to the notice, NaBFID supports infrastructure funding by developing innovative financing instruments, bond and derivatives markets, and data-driven risk management.

Where and How to Send

NaBFID accepts applications for this post only by email. The notice states that no other mode of application will be accepted and hard copies are not to be sent.

  1. Visit the link given against the job position for the detailed role description.
  2. Prepare your CV, including a passport sized photograph.
  3. Send the CV by email to [email protected].
  4. Write the subject line strictly as "APPLICATION FOR THE POST OF <Job Code>". The job code printed for this post is NABFID/EVP/16.
  5. Make sure the email is received on or before 24 November 2026 by 06:00 pm IST.

Candidates should have a valid email ID and keep it active till the declaration of result, as call letters and interview advice will be sent by email.

Posts, Eligibility and Pay

The advertisement covers a single post in the grade of Executive Vice President: Sl. No. 01, EVP & Head- Market Risk, ALM & Enterprise Risk, Job Code NABFID/EVP/16, 1 vacancy (UR).

Educational Qualification

  • Graduate /Postgraduate in any discipline from a recognized University / Institution or a Chartered Account.
  • Preferred: Certification in Financial Risk Management from Global Association of Risk Professionals (GARP) OR Professional Risk Management Certification from PRIMA Institute.

Experience

  • Minimum 20 years of experience in financial sector.
  • Of these, 5 years should be in risk management function (in RBI regulated entity).
  • Of these 5 years, 2 years should be at senior management level.
  • Experience in the infrastructure domain will be preferred.

Age Limit

The age limit is 55 years and below, as on the date of advertisement. After applying all relaxations in terms of age, the maximum age of candidates shall not exceed 55 years. Candidates should satisfy themselves about their eligibility as on the cut-off date, 3 November 2026.

Nationality

The notice invites applications from Indian Citizens.

Pay and Terms of Engagement

  • Remuneration will be offered based on qualifications, experience, suitability, last drawn salary and market benchmark, and shall not be a limiting factor for suitable candidates. No fixed amount is printed in the notice.
  • Contractual engagement will be for a period of 5 years, which may be renewed for additional terms at the discretion of the Bank.
  • Location of position: Mumbai. Selected candidates may be posted in the Bank's establishment in Mumbai/New Delhi/Anywhere in India, as per the Bank's discretion and requirement.
  • Engagement of the selected candidate is subject to being declared medically fit as per the requirement of the Bank.

Candidates should check the detailed role description linked in the official notification for the full eligibility of the post.

NaBFID Recruitment 2026 Job Description

  • Responsible for developing and implementing NaBFID's enterprise-wide risk framework.
  • Ensuring that the Bank's portfolio is built within the defined risk parameters.
  • Building appropriate mechanisms to measure risk.
  • Providing advice and structuring risk mitigation into the business operations at NaBFID.

A detailed role description is available as a separate document on the NaBFID website, linked from the notice.

Enclosures

  • CV including a passport sized photograph (with the email application).
  • No Objection Certificate from the employer at the time of interview, for candidates serving in Govt./Quasi Govt. offices, Public Sector undertakings including Nationalised Banks and Financial Institutions.
  • Details of criminal case(s) pending, if any, at the time of interview.
  • Proper relieving letters from the employer at the time of taking up the appointment, in case of selection.

Selection Process

Applications will be screened and shortlisted on the basis of eligibility and relevant experience, and the requisite number of shortlisted candidates will be called for interview.

  • Screening and shortlisting: based on eligibility and relevant experience. Merely satisfying the eligibility norms does not entitle a candidate to be called for interview.
  • Additional assessment: shortlisted candidates may undergo psychometric tests and/or assessment centre and/or any other selection method deemed suitable by NaBFID, in addition to the personal interview.
  • Personal Interview: conducted by a committee constituted for this purpose.
  • Final selection: made on the basis of eligibility, experience, qualification and performance during the Personal Interview. Selection is solely at the discretion of NaBFID's Selection Committee, and its decision will be final.

The intimation or call letter for interview will be sent by email or uploaded to the Bank's website. No hard copy of the interview letter will be shared.

About SBI Risk Specialist Recruitment

The Central Recruitment & Promotion Department of the State Bank of India, located at the Corporate Centre in Mumbai, conducts regular recruitment for specialist cadre officers. This recruitment cycle invites applications for the Risk Specialist position under Middle Management Grade Scale-II (MMGS-II) to handle expected credit loss modelling, macroeconomic overlays, and model risk management.

The recruitment offers a total of 3 regular vacancies for the Risk Specialist post under the Unreserved (UR) category (with PwBD-VI horizontal reservation of 1 vacancy). The post-wise and category-wise break-up is detailed below.

Candidates must fulfill the mandatory educational qualification, age limits, and post-qualification experience requirements as on 31.10.2026.

  • Age Limit: Minimum 25 years and Maximum 35 years as on 31.10.2026. Upper age limit is for unreserved category candidates. Relaxation in upper age limit is available to reserved category candidates as per Govt. of India guidelines (wherever applicable).
  • Essential Qualification: Mandatory: (i) CA or (ii) CFA or (iii) MBA / PGDM or equivalent degree in Finance / Data Analytics / Business Analytics from a recognized institute.
  • Preferred Qualification / Certification: Financial Risk Manager (FRM) by GARP OR Professional Risk Managers by PRMIA (valid as on 31.10.2026).
  • Work Experience: Minimum 2 years of post-qualification work experience in dealing with Expected Credit Loss (ECL) related modelling in Risk Management Department of any Bank / Financial Institution / Rating Agency / Brokerage firm or Risk Advisory in Consulting Firm as on 31.10.2026. Training & teaching experience will not be counted for eligibility.

Pay and Tenure

Selected candidates are appointed in Middle Management Grade Scale-II (MMGS-II) on a regular basis with a basic pay scale of 64820-2340/1-67160-2680/10-93960. The official will be eligible for DA, HRA, CCA, Provident Fund, Contributory Pension Fund i.e. NPS, Leave Fare Concession (LFC), Medical Facility, other perquisites etc. as per Bank’s salary structure.

SBI Risk Specialist Job Description

Selected candidates will be assigned roles and Key Responsibility Areas (KRAs) that include:

  • Development of Probability of Default (PD), Loss Given Default (LGD) and Exposure at Default (EAD) models for various loan portfolio and investments on which ECL is applicable.
  • Development of Macroeconomic Overlays models required as per regulatory guidelines.
  • Implementation of PD, LGD and EAD Models in OFSAA.
  • Period Monitoring, Maintenance and validation of above models.
  • Preparation of Framework for Determination of Stage under ECL.
  • Identification of Significant Increase in Credit Risk (SICR) triggers along with setting qualitative and quantitative triggers for various portfolio.
  • Coordinate with Auditors & Regulator, BUs & other stakeholders throughout model lifecycle.
  • Maintain proper Model documents and database required for audit & regulatory supervision.
  • Develop models required for ECL computation using industry best practices and using statistical and machine learning techniques.

  6. Verify all filled details carefully before final submission, as no modifications are allowed after final submission.
  7. Pay the application fee online using Internet Banking, Debit Card, or Credit Card.
  8. Save and print the e-receipt and system-generated online application form for future reference.

Selection and Interview

  • Shortlisting: Mere fulfilling the minimum qualification and experience will not vest any right to candidate for being called for interview. The shortlisting committee constituted by the Bank will decide the shortlisting parameters and thereafter, adequate number of candidates, as decided by the Bank, will be shortlisted for interaction.

The mode, date and time of the interview will be communicated to eligible candidates individually. Call letters may be sent to the registered email ID. The Bank's decision on eligibility, conduct of interview and selection will be final.

Bachelor's Degree in Engineering (Computer Science, Information Technology, Electronics and Communication Engineering) or equivalent discipline from a recognised university in India.

  • IS audit experience in banks, financial institutions or regulated entities.
  • Audit exposure in Data Centre, Digital Payment Security, CBS, LOS, mobile banking, internet banking, customer acquisition and management systems, treasury, forex and other banking applications.

  • Patch and vulnerability management.

RRB ALP CBAT Re-Exam 2026 - Which Attempt Will Be Considered?

The rescheduled examination guidance reports specific evaluation rules for candidates who are being offered another attempt because of technical problems during the 30 October 2026 test.

For such candidates, appearing in the 12 November re-examination means that the re-examination performance will be considered in place of the earlier attempt. Candidates who choose not to appear may be evaluated using their original 30 October performance, according to the conditions stated in the rescheduling notice.

These provisions are particularly important for candidates eligible for a repeat attempt. They should read the exact official notice before deciding whether to attend.

Central Railway Apprentice 2026: Railway Recruitment Cell, Central Railway (RRC CR), has released Notification No. RRC/CR/AA/2026 dated 3 November 2026 for engagement of 2,861 Act Apprentices across its Mumbai, Bhusawal, Pune, Nagpur and Solapur clusters. Candidates who have passed Class 10 with at least 50% aggregate marks and possess an NCVT/SCVT certificate in the relevant ITI trade can apply. The age limit is 15 to 24 years as on 3 November 2026, with applicable relaxation. Selected apprentices will receive a stipend of Rs. 9,600 per month during one year of training. The online application process started on 3 November 2026 and closes on 2 December 2026 at 5:00 PM. Eligible candidates can apply online through the official RRC Central Railway website at www.rrccr.com.

Important: This notification is for apprenticeship training under the Apprentices Act, 1961, and does not offer permanent railway employment. Candidates who are currently undergoing or have already completed apprenticeship training should not apply. Applicants must choose only one cluster and ensure their ITI trade has available training slots in the selected units.

Central Railway Act Apprentice 2026 Eligibility Criteria

Candidates must have passed Class 10 with a minimum of 50% aggregate marks from a recognized board and hold an appropriate ITI trade certificate issued or provisionally certified by NCVT/SCVT.

Engineering Degree / Diploma Applicants Not Eligible under This Notification

Important Qualification Restriction: Engineering graduates and diploma holders are not eligible for apprenticeship under this specific notification, as they are covered by a separate apprenticeship scheme. Applicants must satisfy the exact Class 10 and ITI eligibility requirements stated by RRC Central Railway.

Can 10th Pass Candidates Apply Without ITI?

No. Class 10 with at least 50% aggregate marks is required, but candidates must also possess the prescribed ITI trade certificate. A 10th Pass qualification alone does not meet the recruitment eligibility.

Can Candidates Who Have Already Completed Apprenticeship Apply?

No. The notification specifically states that candidates currently undergoing apprenticeship or who have already undergone apprenticeship training should not apply.

Selected Act Apprentices will receive a monthly stipend of Rs. 9,600, as specified under Railway Board RBE No. 116/2025 dated 11 November 2025.

Central Railway Act Apprentice Training Duration 2026

The duration of apprenticeship training is one year for all notified trades. Selected candidates must enter into a Contract of Apprenticeship Training before the programme begins.

Particulars Details

Training Period 1 Year

Apprenticeship Contract Mandatory Before Training
Permanent Employment Guarantee No

For selected applicants who are minors, the apprenticeship contract must be entered into by their guardian. Premature termination of the contract may have consequences under the applicable apprenticeship rules.

Will Central Railway Provide a Permanent Job After Apprenticeship?

No. Central Railway clearly states that completing apprenticeship training does not guarantee employment or automatic absorption into Railway service. The Railway administration is not obligated to provide a permanent job after the training period.

RRC Central Railway Act Apprentice Application Fee 2026

The application fee is Rs. 100 for candidates who are not covered by the notified exemptions. SC, ST, PwBD and women candidates are exempt.

The application fee is non-refundable. Applicable payment transaction charges, if any, must be borne by the candidate.

What If the Application Fee Is Deducted but Payment Is Not Confirmed?

RRC Central Railway advises candidates to use the Verify Payment option if their payment is deducted but the application confirmation cannot be downloaded. Candidates should verify the original transaction before attempting another payment, since duplicate payments may not be refunded.

Central Railway Act Apprentice Selection Process 2026

Selection will be based on a merit list calculated using the simple average of Class 10 and ITI percentage marks. The notification does not prescribe a separate written examination or interview.

  1. Online Application: Candidates apply through the RRC Central Railway website.
  2. Merit Calculation: Class 10 aggregate percentage and ITI percentage are given equal weightage.
  3. Merit List Preparation: Lists are prepared cluster-wise, unit-wise, trade-wise and community-wise.
  4. Document Verification: Shortlisted candidates must produce original educational and category certificates.
  5. Medical Fitness: Candidates must present the prescribed medical fitness certificate.
  6. Apprenticeship Engagement: Eligible candidates are engaged for training after completing the necessary formalities.

Important: Although RRC Central Railway has issued a centralized notification, it will not prepare one centralized merit list for all 2,861 slots. Selection is organized according to the relevant cluster, unit, trade and community.

How Is Central Railway Apprentice Merit Calculated?

The official merit formula is:

Merit Percentage = (Class 10 Aggregate Percentage + ITI Percentage) / 2

Qualification Example Percentage
Class 10 Aggregate Marks 80%
ITI Marks 90%
Calculated Merit Percentage 85%

This is an illustrative calculation, not an actual selection cut-off. Candidates must enter accurate percentages based on the aggregate Class 10 marks and the prescribed consolidated ITI marks.

How Are Grade-Based Class 10 Marks Calculated?

For boards that award letter grades rather than percentages, candidates must calculate the percentage using the midpoint of the marks range corresponding to the overall grade.

If the education board does not issue an overall grade, the midpoints of individual subject-grade ranges must be averaged according to the notification's instructions.

For example, if the overall grade corresponds to the range 80-89%, the midpoint is 84.5%. Candidates should use the conversion instructions given on pages 2 and 3 of the official PDF. Incorrect calculation may lead to rejection during verification.

Central Railway Apprentice Tie-Breaking Rules

If two candidates obtain the same merit percentage, the older candidate will receive preference. If their dates of birth are also identical, the candidate who passed the Matriculation examination earlier will be placed higher.

Is There a Written Exam for Railway Apprentice 2026?

No separate written examination is specified for this Central Railway Act Apprentice engagement. Candidates are shortlisted according to their Class 10 and ITI marks, followed by document verification and medical fitness assessment.

Applicants should not confuse this apprenticeship selection with Railway Recruitment Board (RRB) CBT examinations conducted for regular railway posts.

Central Railway Apprentice Reservation Rules 2026

Reservation applies to eligible SC, ST, OBC, PwBD and Ex-Servicemen categories according to the relevant notification provisions.

SC, ST and OBC Reservation Certificates

SC and ST candidates claiming reservation must upload the appropriate caste certificate in the prescribed Central Government format.

OBC candidates must submit a valid caste certificate and Non-Creamy Layer certificate issued on or after 1 April 2026, in the prescribed Central Government format.

Original certificates must be produced during document verification.

PwBD Eligibility and Reservation

PwBD eligibility is restricted to the disability categories and trade-specific fitness conditions stated in the notification. The applicable provisions include certain locomotor disabilities, cerebral palsy, hearing disabilities and low-vision categories.

Candidates claiming PwBD reservation must possess a valid disability certificate from the competent medical authority. Not every disability category is suitable for every apprenticeship trade, and applicants must check the requirements applicable to their selected trade.

Ex-Servicemen Reservation

The advertisement provides reservation provisions for eligible Ex-Servicemen and certain children of Ex-Servicemen or serving Armed Forces personnel.

Applicants claiming these benefits must upload the required discharge or serving certificate and produce the original supporting documents when called for verification.

Central Railway Apprentice 2026 Apply Online

Candidates can submit online applications through the official RRC Central Railway Apprentice 2026 recruitment portal. The application window is open from 3 November to 2 December 2026.

Direct Apply Online: Central Railway Apprentice 2026 Application Portal

Official Website: www.rrccr.com

Notification Number: RRC/CR/AA/2026.

Last Date: 2 December 2026, 5:00 PM.

Applicants must select only one cluster and may give unit preferences within that cluster. Multiple applications are not permitted and may result in cancellation of all applications submitted by the candidate.

How to Apply Online for Central Railway Apprentice 2026?

  1. Visit the official Railway Recruitment Cell, Central Railway website at www.rrccr.com.
  2. Locate Notification No. RRC/CR/AA/2026 for engagement of Act Apprentices.
  3. Download and read the complete notification before applying.
  4. Check the available ITI trades, cluster-wise vacancies, age criteria and educational requirements.
  5. Click the Apply Online link for the 2026 apprenticeship engagement.
  6. Complete the registration process using the information requested on the portal.
  7. Enter personal details, including name, parents' names, date of birth and contact information.
  8. Provide the required Aadhaar or other permitted identification details.
  9. Enter Class 10 qualification and aggregate percentage marks accurately.
  10. Enter the relevant ITI trade certificate and marks details.
  11. Select only one eligible cluster.
  12. Choose the available units within the selected cluster in order of preference.
  13. Enter the applicable community, reservation and other eligibility details.
  14. Upload the prescribed photograph, signature and supporting certificates.
  15. Review the completed application carefully before final submission.
  16. Pay the application fee of Rs. 100, unless exempt.
  17. Complete the application process before 2 December 2026 at 5:00 PM.
  18. Download and print the application form and retain the registration number and payment receipt.

Important: Candidates should not submit multiple applications using different mobile numbers, email addresses or personal particulars. RRC Central Railway may reject all applications submitted by the same candidate.

Documents Required for Central Railway Apprentice 2026

Applicants must upload legible scanned copies of the required educational and supporting documents during the online application process.

  • Class 10 or equivalent marksheet.
  • Date-of-birth proof through Matriculation certificate, marksheet or accepted school leaving certificate.
  • Consolidated ITI marksheet covering all semesters of the notified trade.
  • National Trade Certificate issued by NCVT or accepted provisional certificate issued by NCVT/SCVT.
  • SC/ST/OBC caste certificate, where applicable.
  • Valid OBC Non-Creamy Layer certificate, where applicable.
  • Disability certificate for eligible PwBD applicants.
  • Discharge certificate or Armed Forces serving certificate for applicable Ex-Servicemen reservation claims.
  • Prescribed recent colour photograph.
  • Scanned candidate signature.
  • Aadhaar or other permitted identity document details.

Original documents must be produced during document verification. Documents issued in languages other than Hindi or English must be accompanied by the required attested translation.

Central Railway Apprentice Photograph and Signature Size

Document Format Dimensions File Size
Photograph JPG / JPEG 3.5 cm x 3.5 cm 20 KB - 70 KB
Signature JPG / JPEG 3.5 cm x 3.5 cm 20 KB - 30 KB

Both images must follow the prescribed 100 DPI specification. The colour photograph must have been taken within three months before application and should show the candidate's face clearly without a cap or sunglasses.

Applicants should retain two additional copies of the same photograph for document verification.

Aadhaar and Identity Requirements for RRC CR Apprentice 2026

Applicants are generally required to enter their 12-digit Aadhaar number during registration. Those who have applied for Aadhaar but have not received the card may enter the 28-digit Aadhaar Enrolment ID.

The notification provides special identification provisions for applicants from Jammu & Kashmir, Meghalaya and Assam. Eligible applicants from these locations may use a permitted Government identity document such as Voter ID, valid passport or driving licence.

The original accepted identification document must be produced during document verification.

Central Railway Apprentice Document Verification 2026

Candidates shortlisted through the merit process will be called for document verification in the relevant division or unit according to their selected cluster.

They must produce the original educational certificates, ITI marksheets, reservation certificates, identity documents and other applicable records.

Medical Fitness Certificate

Shortlisted candidates must bring the prescribed medical fitness certificate in the format provided in Annexure VII of the official notification.

The certificate must be signed by a Government-authorized Gazetted medical officer not below the rank of Assistant Surgeon in a Central or State Government hospital.

Important: Candidates who fail to produce the required medical fitness certificate may not be permitted to undergo document verification and may have their candidature cancelled.

Common Reasons for Rejection of Railway Apprentice Applications

Applicants should carefully review the following requirements because errors may lead to rejection:

  • Not meeting the minimum Class 10 aggregate marks or prescribed ITI qualification.
  • Selecting a unit where no training slots are available for the applicant's ITI trade.
  • Submitting more than one application.
  • Entering incorrect Class 10 or ITI percentages.
  • Providing personal details that do not match the Matriculation certificate.
  • Uploading unclear, corrupt or incorrect documents.
  • Failing to produce the required original certificates during verification.
  • Claiming reservation without the prescribed supporting certificates.
  • Not meeting the applicable age limit.
  • Failing to produce the required medical fitness certificate.
  • Providing false or misleading information.

Applicants should check the complete notification and all entered information before paying the fee and submitting the final application, as editing is not permitted after final submission.

  • Candidates already undergoing or having completed apprenticeship should not apply.
  • Applicants must select only one cluster.

  • Selection is based on the simple average of Class 10 and ITI marks.
  • No separate written examination is prescribed.
  • Merit lists are prepared cluster-wise, unit-wise, trade-wise and community-wise.

  • The notified monthly stipend is Rs. 9,600.
  • The apprenticeship training duration is one year.
  • Selected candidates must arrange their own accommodation.
  • Original document verification and medical fitness are mandatory.
  • No TA/DA will be paid for attending document verification.
  • Apprenticeship completion does not guarantee regular railway employment.
  • Candidates should regularly check the official RRC Central Railway website for updates.

The recruitment process consists of two Computer Based Tests, followed by document verification and medical examination. Unlike several previous NTPC recruitment cycles, CEN 07/2026 does not require a separate Computer Based Typing Skill Test for Junior Clerk cum Typist or Accounts Clerk cum Typist.

  2. CBT-2: Second-stage Computer Based Test for shortlisted candidates.
  3. Document Verification: Verification of original educational, identity, category and other required documents.
  4. Medical Examination: Candidates must pass the prescribed medical fitness standard for their allotted post.

No. The Computer Based Typing Skill Test for Junior Clerk cum Typist and Accounts Clerk cum Typist has been dispensed with under CEN 07/2026. Candidates are still expected to possess basic computer and adequate typing proficiency, which may be assessed after joining.

RailTel Corporation of India Ltd., a Navratna Central Public Sector Enterprise under the Government of India (Ministry of Railways), is inviting applications for 1 post of Advisor (Signalling) – Northern Region/ Delhi NCR on contract under Vacancy Notice No. 20/2026. The post is open only to ex-IRSSE cadre officers retired from Level-14 or above in the CDA Pay matrix (7th CPC). The typed application must be sent to the Sr DGM/HR at RailTel's New Delhi office and must be received by 5 December 2026.

The official notification does not specify the application fee.

About RailTel

RailTel is a "Navratna" Central Public Sector Enterprise and an ICT provider. The notice describes it as one of the largest neutral telecom infrastructure providers in the country, owning a Pan-India optic fiber network laid along railway tracks, and as a listed company aiming to modernise the telecom system for train control, operation and safety. Its registered and corporate office is at East Kidwai Nagar, New Delhi.

Through its strategic relationship with the Indian Railways, RailTel undertakes projects such as IP based video surveillance at stations, 'e-Office' services and short haul and long haul connectivity, and also provides passenger services including content on demand and Wi-Fi at major railway stations.

Where and How to Send

The application must be neatly typed on A-4 size paper in the format prescribed by RailTel and addressed and sent to:

Sr DGM/HR, RailTel Corporation of India Ltd., Plate-A, 6th Floor, Office Block, Tower-2, East Kidwai Nagar, New Delhi-110023

  1. Type the application neatly on A-4 size paper in the format prescribed in the notice.
  2. Sign the application and make sure it is complete in all respects.
  3. Attach self-attested photocopies of the documents listed under Enclosures below.
  4. Superscribe the application as "Application for the post of Advisor (Signalling) - Northern Region".
  5. Send it to the address above so that it reaches the office by 05-12-2026.

The notice does not mention a particular postal mode (speed post, registered post or by hand).

Posts, Eligibility and Pay

RailTel is seeking a dynamic, experienced and result-oriented ex-IRSSE cadre officer with good experience of working in Railway Signalling, including Planning, Design, Maintenance, Construction, Training, Estimate/Tender, along with EPC contract exposure pertaining to Railway Signaling Infrastructure.

  • Post and vacancies: Advisor (Signalling) – Northern Region/ Delhi NCR, 01 post.
  • Eligibility: IRSSE officer retired from Level-14 or above in CDA Pay matrix (7th CPC).
  • Educational qualification: The official notification does not specify the minimum educational qualification.
  • Experience: More than 30 years of working experience in Railway Signalling including Planning, Design, Maintenance, Construction, Training, Estimate/Tender along with EPC contract exposure pertaining to Railway Signaling Infrastructure.
  • Age limit: The applicant should not be more than 62 years of age as on the closing date of application.
  • Compensation: Consolidated lump sum payment per month will be equal to Last Pay + DA drawn minus Pension (before commutation).
  • Contract duration: The engagement shall initially be for a period of one year, extendable based on organizational requirement, performance and mutual consent, subject to the maximum prescribed age limit, whichever is earlier.

Candidates should check the official notification for the complete eligibility conditions of the post.

Enclosures

Self-attested photocopies of the following documents must accompany the application:

  • Pay Pension Order (P.P.O)
  • Service Certificate issued by previous employer at the time of retirement
  • One page write-up of work handled, including significant achievements, if any
  • Address of the Vigilance Department of the previous employer for collecting D&AR and Vigilance Clearance

An application not accompanied by the P.P.O, the Service Certificate and the address of the previous employer's Vigilance Department, and any incomplete or vague application, will be rejected summarily.

Selection Process

Selection for the Advisor (Signalling) post shall be based on scrutiny of applications and a personal interview.

  • Scrutiny of applications: the applications received are examined first.
  • Personal Interview: the second stage of selection.
  • Vigilance clearance: shall be obtained from the organization from which the applicant retired.
  • Medical examination: selected candidates will have to undergo a medical examination/health check-up and will be considered for engagement as Consultant/Advisor only if found medically fit.

The notice does not give an interview date or venue.

Is the Rajasthan SET Final Answer Key 2026 Out?

Yes, according to a published on 6 November 2026. The University of Kota has published subject-wise final answer keys on the SET result page of its official website. Candidates should open uok.ac.in and confirm the latest notice before relying on any third-party page.

The final answer key is prepared after the university reviews the objections received against the provisional key. Candidates cannot assume that every answer from the 5 October key remains unchanged, so recheck your answers against the final version.

How to Download the Rajasthan SET Final Answer Key 2026

  1. Visit the official University of Kota website at uok.ac.in.
  2. Open the SET Examination 2026 section.
  3. Look for the result and final answer key link.
  4. Select your subject from the list.
  5. The subject-wise PDF will open. No login is required for the Master Set PDFs on the university page.

Rajasthan SET 2026 Exam Pattern and Marking Scheme

Paper Subject Questions Marks Duration
Paper I Teaching and Research Aptitude (General) 50 100 1 hour
Paper II Candidate's chosen subject 100 200 2 hours
  • All questions are multiple choice and compulsory.
  • Each correct answer carries 2 marks.
  • There is no negative marking.
  • There is no break between the two papers.
  • The exam was held in a single session from 11:00 AM to 2:00 PM.

How to Check Your Expected Score Using the Answer Key

  1. Download the final answer key for your subject.
  2. Match each of your marked answers with the key.
  3. Give 2 marks for every correct answer.
  4. Do not deduct marks for wrong or unattempted questions.
  5. Add up the marks for Paper I and Paper II.

This gives only an expected score. Your official marks and qualifying status are decided by the University of Kota in the result.

  • Download and save the result and answer key PDFs.
  • Read the official notice for certificate or document-related instructions, if any are issued.
  • Candidates of the re-exam centres should follow the re-examination notice.

Important Instructions for Candidates

  • Do not rely on unofficial dates or messages on social media.

The provisional answers are available through the Master Question Paper on the official UPESSC website. The objection window is open from 5 November to 12 November 2026. Candidates can log in with their roll number and date of birth to check the answer key for their paper and booklet series and to challenge any answer they believe is wrong.

UP Special TET Answer Key 2026 Important Dates

The exam was held on 3 November 2026 and the objection window began on 5 November 2026. Candidates should raise all objections on or before 12 November 2026.

UP Special TET 2026 Exam 3 November 2026
Provisional Answer Key and Objection Window Opens 5 November 2026

UP Special TET Answer Key 2026 PDF Download

The answer keys for Paper 1 and Paper 2 are available separately, and each is arranged by booklet series. Candidates should open the key that matches the paper they appeared in and the series code printed on their question booklet. Checking against the wrong series is the most common reason for a wrong score estimate.

How to Download the UP Special TET Answer Key 2026

  1. Visit the official UPESSC website at upessc.up.gov.in.
  2. Open the UP Special TET exam portal tab on the homepage.
  3. Log in with your roll number and date of birth.
  4. Click the link for the UP Special TET provisional answer key 2026.
  5. Select your paper, Paper 1 or Paper 2.
  6. Choose your booklet series code: A, B, C or D.
  7. Open the PDF, then download and save it for reference.

How to Raise Objection Against UP Special TET Answer Key 2026

Objections are accepted only through the online objection window on the official UPESSC portal. A valid justification or reference is required for every question you challenge.

  1. Open the official UPESSC website and go to the UP Special TET 2026 objection portal.
  2. Log in with your roll number and date of birth in DDMMYYYY format.
  3. Select the question you want to challenge.
  4. Choose the objection type from the dropdown menu shown against that question.
  5. Enter a valid justification or reference in the text box.
  6. Submit one or more objections, then check them under the View Objection Summary option. You can print the summary using the print icon.
  7. Pay the prescribed fee online through the payment option under the View Objection Summary tab.

UP Special TET Answer Key Objection Fee

The objection fee is payable per question and online. Two different amounts are in circulation: ₹100 per question and approximately ₹500 per question. The amount is Not Confirmed Officially on this page. Pay only the amount displayed on the objection portal at the time of submission, and keep the payment confirmation until the final answer key is published.

What to Attach or Mention as Proof

Support each objection with a clear justification and a reference, such as a page from a standard NCERT or SCERT textbook. A specific reference is more useful to the review than a general statement that the answer is wrong.

How to Calculate Your Probable Score Using the UP Special TET Answer Key

  1. Download the key for your paper and your booklet series.
  2. Compare each of your marked answers with the provisional key.
  3. Award 1 mark for every correct answer.
  4. Do not deduct marks for wrong or unattempted questions, as there is no negative marking.
  5. Add up the marks. Your total is out of 150.

Important Instructions for Candidates

  • Check the answer key of your own paper and your own booklet series only.
  • Raise objections only within the window, which ends on 12 November 2026.
  • Give a specific justification and reference for every objection.
  • Check the fee shown on the portal before paying, and save the payment receipt and objection summary.
  • Use only the official UPESSC website. Do not enter login details on any other page.
  • Treat your probable score as an estimate until the final answer key and result are published.

How to Calculate Marks Using DSSSB Answer Key 2026?

Candidates may use their available examination responses and the draft answer key to estimate their performance. However, they must apply the marking scheme prescribed for their specific DSSSB post and examination.

Provisional Answer Key vs Final Answer Key

The provisional key was released on 5 October 2026 so candidates could compare their answers and raise objections. After reviewing the objections, GSSSB issued the final key. The final key carries corrections for some questions based on expert review and supporting documents submitted by candidates.

About UPSC Indian Statistical Service (ISS) Examination 2026

The ISS Examination is one of the premier competitive exams conducted by UPSC to recruit officers for Group A and Group B posts in the Indian Statistical Service. Understanding the exam structure helps candidates correctly interpret the provisional answer key.

The Indian Statistical Service (ISS) Examination is conducted annually by the Union Public Service Commission to fill vacancies in the Indian Statistical Service, one of India's organised Group A Central Services. The exam tests candidates on subjects including Statistics, General English, and General Studies. The Statistics papers are the most technical and weightage-heavy components of the exam. The provisional answer key released covers the objective/multiple-choice components of the Statistics papers.

ISS Examination Paper Structure

The ISS Examination 2026 Statistics papers for which the provisional answer key has been released are:

How to Raise Objections Against UPSC ISS Provisional Answer Key 2026

If a candidate disagrees with any answer published in the provisional answer key, they can submit a formal representation to UPSC within the stipulated objection window period.

  • Download the provisional answer key PDF for the relevant paper.
  • Identify the question number(s) where you believe the answer is incorrect.
  • Prepare a written representation with supporting references from standard textbooks or study material.
  • Submit the representation to UPSC through the official channel specified in the answer key notification (typically by post or online submission to the UPSC office).
  • UPSC will review all representations received before publishing the Final Answer Key.

What Happens After the Provisional Answer Key?

After the provisional answer key is released and the objection window closes, UPSC reviews all valid representations before publishing the Final Answer Key.

Once the objection period ends, UPSC's subject matter experts review all representations submitted by candidates. Valid objections where an answer is found to be incorrect based on credible references result in changes to the final answer key. The Final Answer Key is then published on the official website. The final marks are computed based on the final (not provisional) answer key, which forms the basis for merit list preparation and eventual selection to the Indian Statistical Service.

SSC Selection Post Phase 14 Answer Key 2026 - Quick Overview

The SSC Selection Post Phase 14 answer key is the tentative answer key for the Phase-XIV/2026 computer-based exam. Candidates log in to the SSC portal, view their own response sheet next to the key, and can challenge answers by paying a fee per question before the window closes.
